query: One enterprise customer says exports are failing for them, but our dashboards look basically fine and nobody else has complained. Is this a SEV1 or a SEV2 or not even an incident? I do not want to overreact.
expected_behavior: Resolves the ambiguity by rounding up rather than down: when it sits between two levels, declares the higher severity and downgrades later once impact is clear
First confirms the actual blast radius (is it only this customer, is data being lost, is it spreading) before locking the severity, instead of guessing from the dashboard
Explains that under-declaring is more expensive than over-declaring because the cost is asymmetric, so bias upward
States that severity can be downgraded explicitly and logged once impact is proven smaller, so calling it high now is safe and reversible
Does not dismiss it as a non-incident purely because dashboards look healthy, since a single customer with active data loss can still be high severity
